source.title: High dimensional analysis reveals conservative sharpening and a stochastic edge of stability

record.tranche_reason: Tests batch size effects on test error using a different setup and measure from the version's cited studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports training-loss and stability results, but those do not measure the training–test gap. The CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 batch-size sweep reports final test error and bears on V5. Other version-specific findings in the paper are theoretical or concern training outcomes, not the generalization behaviors named in those versions.
record.test_reason: The fixed-200-epoch ResNet18/CIFAR10 batch-size sweep measures final test error under a learning-rate scaling recipe and bears on V5 in a new training setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Appendix D.2 but not the paper's overall conclusion. The authors conclude that SGD has a stochastic edge of stability characterized by a noise kernel norm, that conservative sharpening suppresses eigenvalue growth, and that intermediate noise levels predict better training outcomes. The batch-size sweep reports similar final test error at constant η/B over a range, with consistency breaking down at large η/B and larger batches.
record.recipe_differences: ResNet18 on CIFAR10 with MSE loss, momentum, cosine learning-rate schedule, and L2 regularization; 200 epochs and a sweep over batch size and η/B.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported batch-size consistency depends on η/B and breaks down for larger batch sizes and larger η/B.

fits_no_version.finding: Noise kernel norm K predicts optimization behavior and, in some experiments, held-out error across learning rates; conservative sharpening changes Hessian/NTK eigenvalue dynamics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD noise and stochastic stability measures predict training outcomes in certain regimes. These measurements do not test magnitude-aware sharpness against the training–test gap.

record.problems: The final test-error values are presented in a figure without recoverable exact numbers; the text gives only a qualitative comparison. The batch-size sweep also varies η/B.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the other versions: their relevant generalization outcomes are not measured. Training-loss and stability results do not measure the training–test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy.
Held-out error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Language models; unadapted learning-rate comparisons; longer training; controlled effects of warmup, normalization, or regularization changes; batches above 256.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness versus training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text establishes parity qualitatively but does not establish whether the breakdown region has higher or lower test error. No directional verdict is justified for that region. This study is not an original source for V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Language models; comparison at fixed epochs without recipe adaptation; effects of longer training, warmup, normalization, and regularization changes.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness tracks the training–test gap.
Whether removing memorized training examples reduces test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained across batch sizes and normalized base learning rates; compared median estimated noise kernel norm and final test error.
rows.note: Authors state that final test error is similar across batch sizes for constant η/B, with consistency breaking down at large η/B and larger batch size. Figure does not provide recoverable exact values.
rows.check: For the conditions described as having similar test error at constant η/B, the batch-size penalty is absent, not partial. The baseline is smaller batches at the same η/B and epoch budget; absolute learning rate scales with batch size. Split these conditions from the large-batch/large-η/B breakdown region, whose direction and magnitude cannot be established from the supplied figure text. Add layer normalization, GeLU, momentum 0.9, cosine scheduling, and L2 coefficient 5×10^-4 to the conditions.

relationships.condition: ResNet18/CIFAR10, 200 epochs, batch sizes within the constant-η/B consistency regime, with learning rate scaled linearly with batch size
relationships.reason: R1: Appendix D.2 explicitly reports similar final test error across batch sizes, supporting V5's qualification that an adapted recipe can avoid the penalty within the same epoch budget.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports similar final test error across batch sizes when the learning rate was scaled in proportion to batch size, but this comparison remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
